messages:
incident-bot: [SEV2] Dedicated pool eu-west-1 saturating — queue depth > 1200, p95 gen latency >= 2.4s, p99 >= 9.1s. Affected routes: /v1/chat/stream. Paging oncall.
clare: saw the alert. I'm oncall. looking at dashboard now — 95% GPU utilization on pool-redwood-dedicated-eu-3 and warmup failures spiking.
anand: noticed autoscaler add-node requests are queued at the cloud API level. cloud returned 429 for node create for last 3 minutes.
jamie: streaming stalls correlate with KV cache miss rate jumping from 3% -> 42% during the burst. tail latency likely caused by cold kvcalls plus queue amplification.
clare: customer visible p95s are up; CS pinged. @liu can you confirm customer impact / any big tenants? we might need live page.
liu: customer-ops: 3 customers reported degraded responses, two are high-Tier. They're reporting streaming cutouts and long initial token delays. escalating to account managers.
clare: step 1: reduce inflight batch sizes to limit queue depth and lower per-token latency. applying flag now.
jamie: flag applied: ```runtime.config.batch.max_inflight_per_worker=8``` — pushing to all eu workers. watching.
anand: cloud API 429s due to quota throttle; requesting emergency quota bump — already on support ticket with provider. ETA unknown.
carla: can we spin up a fallback CPU-backed hotshot pool to soak some infer requests for non-streaming routes? might help immediate SLOs.
clare: good idea. jamie, can runtime route low-priority text-gen to fallback-quant-cpu? risk is higher latency but avoids p99 streaming stalls.
jamie: yes, we have model-variant 'llama-13b-quant-cpu' ready. applying routing rule for priority<=low. ```routing.v1.set({route:\"/v1/generate\", priority_threshold:\"low\", target_pool:\"fallback-cpu-eu\"})```.
anand: started provisioning fallback-cpu-eu via infra CLI; note: it takes ~40s per instance to become ready. parallel create 6 instances.
clare: updating oncall-manager: live page will remain open. assigning action owners: infra/anand for cloud quotas, runtime/jamie for routing & cache mitigations, oncall/clare for customer updates.
oncall-manager: acknowledged. escalate if p99 stays > 5s for next 10m.
jamie: also enabling aggressive KV prewarm for hot prefixes. ```kv.prewarm.enable = true; kv.prewarm.window = 60s``` — targeting top 50 keys.
clare: metrics after batch change: queue depth down from 1250 -> 480 in 90s, p95 decreased to 1.1s, p99 still 6.3s. streaming stalls reduced but not gone.
liu: customer-ops: initial customer reports show partial recovery for one tenant, second still seeing stalls.
anand: fallback-cpu-eu nodes reported ready. We routed low-priority traffic. observing latency on fallback pool ~2.5s p95 but stable. should offload load now.
clare: traffic shift in effect. overall queue depth 260. p95 now 0.95s, p99 3.2s. still borderline but improving.
jamie: root-cause sketch: burst of traffic with many cold KV prefixes triggered warmup storms; autoscaler delayed due to provider-side quota throttles and instance creation API retries, causing sustained queue growth and streaming tail amplification.
clare: next steps: 1) keep routing in place until quota bump lands or dedicated nodes finish warmup; 2) add short-term client throttling for untagged bursts; 3) post-incident analysis to tune warmup and handshake backoff.
anand: cloud support replied: provisional quota bump granted +200 instances in eu-west-1, provisioning continues. ETA 7m.
carla: note for postmortem: consider adding a fast-path for function-calling or short-streams to use warm pools only; avoid cold-kv on first token where possible.
clare: customer comms: @liu please send update: we mitigated majority of impact, fallback routing active, team is provisioning capacity and investigating autoscaler retries. ETA next update in 10m.
liu: sending update now. message: "We're seeing improved performance; working on restoring full SLA. We'll follow up in 10 minutes with next status." :thumbsup:
anand: autoscaler logs show repeated 502s from cloud create endpoint; adding exponential backoff + jitter to our controller to avoid hammering.
jamie: also lowering cold-start penalties: reduce cache eviction aggressiveness during warmup windows and prioritize KV prefetch for known hot prefixes.
clare: monitoring for 15m. if p99 < 1s and queue < 100 we'll close page. current p99 2.1s, queue 140.
oncall-manager: if anything customer-impacting again, escalate to SEV1. otherwise continue with mitigation playbook and schedule postmortem.
clare: after 12m more, p95 0.9s, p99 0.95s, queue depth 45. autoscaler provisioning completed additional 12 nodes; warmup metrics show KV hit rate back to ~6% miss.
clare: closing live page in 5. thanks everyone for quick coordination. will file postmortem and include traffic pattern, autoscaler retry behavior, and warmup optimizations.
liu: sent customer final update: "Full service restored, investigating root cause and next steps; will share postmortem timeline." customers acknowledged.
jamie: adding follow-ups: change default batch size heuristics to be workload-aware during bursts; add circuit breaker on autoscaler retries to avoid API backpressure.
anand: raising infra ticket for quota monitoring alerts and provider rate-limit handling improvements.
clare: end-of-thread notes: incident started at 7812345678, mitigations: batch reduction, fallback CPU pool, KV prewarm, routing changes, autoscaler backoff fixes; owner list: clare (oncall), anand (infra), jamie (runtime), liu (CS). postmortem ETA 72h. :white_check_mark:
